function: Sensing channel estimation in ISAC: a Brownian-bridge diffusion network denoises the least-squares estimate of the transmit-BS-target-receive-BS channel matrix (pp. 3-5).
system: Distributed massive MIMO ISAC: transmitting and receiving BS with N=32-element ULAs, K UEs, L point-like targets; narrowband; no RIS; carrier frequency not stated (pp. 3, 8).
method: Brownian-bridge diffusion model (T=10) with U-Net, attention and time embedding after DFT virtual-channel preprocessing; trained offline, 160 epochs, Adam, on paired LS and true channels (pp. 6-9).
data_channel: Own Monte-Carlo scatter-channel simulator: Poisson(3) targets, uniform angles, complex Gaussian gains; 7500 training and 2500 testing instances; no standard model or dataset (pp. 3, 8).
test_conditions: Same simulator, N=32, for training and testing; 7500 training and 2500 held-out instances; SNR sweep -10 to 10 dB; no new scenario (pp. 8-9).
baselines: LS, LMMSE (non-learned); DnCNN, cGAN, U-Net (learned; U-Net is the ablation without diffusion) (pp. 9-11).
metrics: Normalized mean squared error (NMSE) versus SNR, sampling diversity and number of time steps; training loss convergence; heatmaps of latents (pp. 8-11).
complexity: Inference FLOPs O(T N^2), overall O(N^3 + T N^2); training O(E N^2); LMMSE O(N^6); no runtime or parameter count (p. 8).
q1_support: p. 3: "we adopt the scatter channel model [3] in this work"; p. 8: "Monte-Carlo simulations are employed to generate the dataset". Custom simulator; no 3GPP model, DeepMIMO or measured data.
q2_support: p. 8: "7500 instances utilized as the training set and 2500 instances utilized as the testing set", a held-out part of the same simulator. The SNR sweep (Fig. 5) does not count; no other N, number of targets or scenario is tested.
q3_support: p. 9: "we compare our proposed method with LS, LMMSE, DnCNN [19], [20], cGAN [30], and U-Net [43] channel estimation methods" on NMSE (Fig. 5).
q4_support: p. 8: "In the online inference phase, the required FLOPs are" O(T N^2), overall O(N^3 + T N^2), "significantly lower than that of the LMMSE channel estimation" with O(N^6).
q5_support: p. 8: "Monte-Carlo simulations are employed to generate the dataset". The paper gives no code or data link and uses no public dataset.
notes: Area 2 because channel estimation in an ISAC system is area 2; the system also communicates (K UEs, p. 3), so the sensing-alone exclusion does not apply. The U-Net baseline is an ablation (same network without the diffusion process, p. 9) and was not counted as the learned baseline; DnCNN and cGAN count. "Generalizes well to unseen data" (p. 9) refers to the held-out test set of the same simulator. Table I was read from the page image (p. 9).
